name: Slovenian nationalism
summary: Slovenian nationalism holds that Slovenes are a distinct nation with a permanent right to self-determination and their own sovereign state, language and culture, a cause that ran from the 19th-century national awakening through the May Declaration to independence in 1991. Today it is carried most explicitly by the Slovenian National Party, which stresses sovereignty, armed neutrality, restricted immigration, Slovenes-first social policy, patriotic education and the protection of Slovene minorities abroad.
scope: Slovenian nationalism from the 1987-1991 independence movement (May Declaration, Basic Constitutional Charter, Constitution) to the programmes of the Slovenian National Party (SNS), which scholarship calls the representative of Slovenian nationalism. Only positions about the nation, sovereignty, immigration, minorities, language, culture and foreign policy are answered; economics, social morality and other themes are null, since the sources record them only as one party's platform. The wartime Home Guard and the wider conservative right are not modelled.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Constitution's preamble and Article 3 found the state on the permanent and inalienable right of the Slovene nation to self-determination, and the May Declaration demanded a sovereign state of the Slovene nation.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Article 5 of the Constitution commits the state to concern for autochthonous Slovene minorities in neighbouring countries and for emigrants, and the SNS programme pledges help to the Slovene minorities in Austria, Italy, Hungary and Croatia.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The SNS programme makes preserving Slovene culture, customs, language and historical heritage a core aim, and Article 5 charges the state with preserving cultural heritage.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The SNS programme asserts the undisputed indigenous presence of the Slovene nation from the Veneti through Carantania to today and rejects the sixth-century migration account; the scholarship notes the Carantanian myth as central to Slovene national identity.

nation-first.rationale: The SNS programmes put Slovenes first and warn that dependence on the EU and NATO has eroded independence, while accepting only pragmatic cooperation for Slovenia's benefit.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The SNS programmes want a Europe of nations rather than the EU, and the 2026 programme demands a looser association without transfer of key sovereign powers (SLOexit if reform fails); the strand around the SNS is the only one documented in the opened sources.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The 2026 SNS programme calls for leaving the United Nations because it limits sovereign decision-making and pushes globalist agendas.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The SNS programme demands armed neutrality outside all military alliances and leaving NATO.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The SNS programme calls for a defence policy of armed neutrality outside all military alliances.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The SNS programme refuses any NATO military bases on Slovene territory.

conscription.rationale: The SNS programmes call for reintroducing compulsory military service, in 2026 for men and women aged 18 to 27 with a civilian alternative.

empower-police-military.rationale: The SNS programmes ask for more police, better police pay and a properly equipped army, though not wider powers.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The SNS programmes limit employment of foreigners to the lowest quotas, fully block illegal migration and restrict legal migration to stated economic needs; the scholarship describes its programme as strict measures against immigrants from the start.

open-borders.rationale: The SNS programmes oppose the migrant flow and demand strict border control, criminalising illegal crossing.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The SNS programmes put social security first for Slovenes, treat foreigners as outside labour and in 2026 end transfers to foreigners without five years' residence; the scholarship records the same aim.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The 2026 SNS programme states that foreigners who are not citizens cannot vote in local elections.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The 2026 SNS programme demands ending all military, humanitarian and development aid abroad except for emergencies on or next to Slovene borders.

patriotic-education.rationale: The 2026 SNS programme requires compulsory patriotic education teaching the nation's history, anthem, flag and pride in statehood.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The 2026 SNS programme builds the compulsory patriotic curriculum on the history of the Slovene nation and its heroes; it does not say the nation must be the centre of all school history.

single-official-language.rationale: Strands differ: the 1991 Constitution (Article 11) makes Slovene official while keeping Italian and Hungarian official in their areas, while the 2026 SNS programme makes Slovene the only official language in administration and media.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The 2022 SNS programme makes social transfers conditional on Slovene at B1 level and schools a preparatory year for foreigners.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The 2026 SNS programme states that Islam does not belong in Slovenia and the 2022 programme says illegal migrants came to Islamise European nations.

elite-replacement.rationale: The 2022 SNS programme says Soros-type organisations back the migrant flow that aims to Islamise European nations, close to but not exactly a replacement claim, and a contested view.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The 2026 SNS programme pays Slovene families more per child to raise births and stabilise demography while restricting immigration.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The 2022 SNS programme opposes sales of profitable Slovene firms to foreign buyers and wants foreign capital controlled by Slovene law, without naming strategic industries.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The SNS programme makes funding museums and restoring heritage buildings a priority.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Constitution and the SNS programme treat Slovenes in Austria, Italy, Hungary and Croatia as part of the Slovene nation across state borders.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Sources point both ways: the Constitution calls Slovenia a state of all its citizens, the scholarship notes civic nationalism in the independence movement, while the SNS aimed at Slovenia for Slovenes and limits membership to ethnic Slovenes.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Strands differ: the SNS was irredentist about Carinthia, Istria and Friuli (and its 2022 programme restores 1918 statehood), while the 1991 Charter fixed the existing borders.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Strands differ: the SNS pursued a Greater Slovenia incorporating neighbouring Slovene lands, while the 1991 Charter accepted the existing borders.
